papers.title: A latent control model for realistic rodent motion
papers.reason: The paper is a pure simulated-agent rodent locomotor-control system rather than a human or animal study or a model of executive cognition.

papers.title: Does Sports Participation Buffer the Cognitive Cost of Academic Stress? A Moderated Mediation Analysis of Concentration and Intelligence among Indian Adolescents
papers.reason: The study examines concentration as a behavioural cognitive mechanism in adolescents, but its main contribution is a stress and sports participation mediation analysis rather than executive-function modelling.

papers.title: Subjective emotional ratings dissociate brain activation and network patterns during counterfactual outcome processing.
papers.reason: It reports human fMRI and behavioural findings on counterfactual outcome evaluation, regret, OFC activation, and decision traits that could inform computational models of decision making.

papers.title: Chunking: What working memory gains and loses.
papers.reason: The title indicates a central treatment of chunking in working memory, although the absence of an abstract prevents judging whether it includes computational modelling.

papers.title: Mental Workload: Physiological Assessment and Validation Using Visual Stimuli
papers.reason: The paper uses EEG features and an SVM classifier to assess workload during a visual attention and working-memory task, making it relevant to physiological cognitive assessment.

papers.title: Para além da psicopatologia: o papel da organicidade nos comportamentos suicidários inaugurais no idoso
papers.reason: It discusses delirium, sleep deprivation, impulsivity, and prefrontal inhibitory control in elderly suicide risk, but executive cognition is only a peripheral explanatory element.

papers.title: The Influence of the Role of Peer Presence on Game‐Based Chemistry Learning: Evidence From EEG
papers.reason: It reports EEG theta and alpha differences linked to cognitive load, cognitive control, and selective processing, but the core setting is educational game-based chemistry learning.

papers.title: A non-randomized trial of the effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on cognitive performance and resting state connectivity
papers.reason: The study directly tests effects of taVNS on executive-function tasks, adaptive cognitive training, and high-density EEG connectivity in humans.

papers.title: Robot-assisted cognitive assessment with eye-tracking
papers.reason: The title indicates a close methodological match to cognitive assessment using eye tracking, although no abstract is available to judge clinical or executive-function specificity.

papers.title: Feasibility and safety of immersive virtual reality training device (ReMind) in post-stroke rehabilitation
papers.reason: The title suggests clinical rehabilitation technology, but there is no clear evidence of executive-function modelling, cognitive assessment, eye tracking, or EEG.

papers.title: Long-term episodic memory alterations and the role of perceived stress in post-COVID-19 condition.
papers.reason: The study concerns long-term episodic memory and stress in post-COVID cognitive follow-up rather than planning, working memory, attention, executive control, or computational assessment.

papers.title: Validation of the diagnosis of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome: Challenges and lessons learned.
papers.reason: The available record indicates diagnostic validation of an epilepsy syndrome with no evident focus on executive function, computational modelling, or cognitive assessment.

papers.title: Case Report: Sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease initially misdiagnosed as ischemic stroke: a diagnostic challenge and biomarker-based clarification
papers.reason: It is a neurological case report about biomarker-based diagnosis of rapidly progressive dementia, with only general relevance to cognitive impairment detection.

papers.title: Resting-state beta-band oscillatory dysfunction bridges Alzheimer’s pathology and memory impairment
papers.reason: It uses resting-state EEG, PET biomarkers, clinical grouping, and cognitive outcomes in AD-MCI, making it relevant to EEG-based cognitive impairment biomarkers despite its emphasis on memory rather than executive function.
